Write a change table as delimited text, JSON or Markdown

Source: R/yoy_write.R
yoydelim.Rd

yoycsv() separates fields with a comma and quotes any field that contains one; yoytsv() separates with a tab and replaces any tab inside a field, since a tab-separated field cannot contain one and writing it would shift every column after it. yoyjs() writes an object with settings (value, period, grouping, lag, units, minimum base, confidence level, direction), summary (from yoysmry()) and rows, using the package's own JSON codec. yoymd() writes a pipe table meant for reading: values formatted (every numeric column right-aligned), percentages signed and rounded, the interval as [lower, upper], notes in the last column, and the settings in an italic line under the table.

Usage

yoycsv(x, file, digits = NULL, na = "", meta = TRUE, comment = "#", ...)

yoytsv(x, file, digits = NULL, na = "", meta = TRUE, comment = "#", ...)

yoyjs(x, file, digits = NULL, pretty = TRUE, ...)

yoymd(x, file, digits = 1L, align = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

An rmbl_yoy object from yoy().

file

Character scalar, the output path, or NULL to return the text instead of writing it.

digits

A whole number from 0 to 15, or NULL: decimal places for the percent columns. For the CSV, TSV and JSON writers NULL, the default, writes them unrounded, which is what a downstream calculation wants; give a number for a figure meant to be read. For yoymd() the default is 1.

na

Character scalar, how to write a missing value (CSV and TSV). The default empty string is what most readers expect; "NA" keeps R's own spelling.

meta

Whether to lead with comment lines recording the lag, units, confidence level, base gate and direction. On by default, because a percent column means different things under different settings and the file is the only place a later reader can look. Markdown and JSON carry the same information structurally.

comment

Character scalar, the comment prefix for the metadata lines; default "#".

...

Ignored: what yoywr() passes on for its HTML and PDF writers.

pretty

Logical scalar, default TRUE: indent the JSON.

align

Logical scalar, default TRUE: pad the Markdown columns so the source table is readable unrendered.

Value

file, invisibly; or, when file is NULL, the text as a character scalar.

Details

The CSV and TSV writers export every column of the object (the period and grouping columns, value, previous, change, the percent or percentage-point change, flag, the interval and verdict), so the note explaining a missing or flagged figure stays with its row. Quoting in the CSV follows RFC 4180 (a field with a comma, a quote or a line break is quoted, quotes doubled). The metadata line names the value and period columns, the grouping, the lag, the units, and for counts the interval's confidence level and the base below which changes are noted. A pipe inside a Markdown cell is escaped. An existing file is overwritten. Errors when x does not come from yoy(), or digits is not a whole number.

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = 2019:2023, n = c(402, 377, 190, 268, 331))
y <- yoy(d, value = "n", prd = "year")

# Straight to text, for inspection.
cat(yoycsv(y, NULL))
#> # value: n; period: year; lag: 1; units: count; interval: 95% exact rate ratio
#> year,value,previous,change,pctchg,flag,pctlo,pctup,verdict
#> 2019,402,,,,no comparison period,,,
#> 2020,377,402,-25,-6.21890547263682,,-18.7301481792582,8.20024314312362,down
#> 2021,190,377,-187,-49.6021220159151,,-57.8921768223217,-39.8426144902702,down
#> 2022,268,190,78,41.0526315789474,,16.6890230584617,70.7750209773721,up
#> 2023,331,268,63,23.5074626865672,,4.81624015357676,45.6380333585367,up

# Markdown, for a report.
cat(yoymd(y, NULL))
#> | year |   n | previous | change | change % |     interval | note                 |
#> | ---- | --: | -------: | -----: | -------: | -----------: | -------------------- |
#> | 2019 | 402 |        — |      — |        — |              | no comparison period |
#> | 2020 | 377 |      402 |    -25 |    -6.2% |  [-19%, +8%] |                      |
#> | 2021 | 190 |      377 |   -187 |   -49.6% | [-58%, -40%] |                      |
#> | 2022 | 268 |      190 |     78 |   +41.1% | [+17%, +71%] |                      |
#> | 2023 | 331 |      268 |     63 |   +23.5% |  [+5%, +46%] |                      |
#> 
#> _value: n; period: year; lag: 1; units: count; interval: 95% exact rate ratio_

# JSON keeps the settings as fields rather than as comments.
substr(yoyjs(y, NULL), 1, 80)
#> [1] "{\n  \"settings\": {\n    \"value\": \"n\",\n    \"period\": \"year\",\n    \"lag\": 1,\n    \"uni"

# rounded percentages, no metadata line, and R's own NA
cat(yoytsv(y, NULL, digits = 1, meta = FALSE, na = "NA"))
#> year	value	previous	change	pctchg	flag	pctlo	pctup	verdict
#> 2019	402	NA	NA	NA	no comparison period	NA	NA	NA
#> 2020	377	402	-25	-6.2	NA	-18.7	8.2	down
#> 2021	190	377	-187	-49.6	NA	-57.9	-39.8	down
#> 2022	268	190	78	41.1	NA	16.7	70.8	up
#> 2023	331	268	63	23.5	NA	4.8	45.6	up

# written to a file
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
yoycsv(y, f)
read.csv(f, comment.char = "#")[, c("year", "pctchg", "flag")]
#>   year     pctchg                 flag
#> 1 2019         NA no comparison period
#> 2 2020  -6.218905                     
#> 3 2021 -49.602122                     
#> 4 2022  41.052632                     
#> 5 2023  23.507463                     

# only yoy() results are accepted
try(yoycsv(d, NULL))
#> Error : yoycsv: `x` must be an rmbl_yoy object from yoy()
